Answer notes
For the intact bull call example, maximum expiration loss before costs is: Options: Unlimited; The width of the spread; The $200 net debit; The strike price. Correct answer: The $200 net debit. Why: Both calls expire worthless below $180, leaving the $200 debit as the gross loss. Costs and separate stock exposure are excluded.
An intact short iron condor has its maximum gross expiration gain when the underlying: Options: Rallies sharply beyond the upper wing; Crashes beyond the lower wing; Finishes between the short strikes; Goes to zero. Correct answer: Finishes between the short strikes. Why: The four options expire without intrinsic value between the short strikes, leaving the credit before costs.
In the worksheet, 1-2% of a hypothetical $100,000 account equals: Options: $50,000; $25,000; $1,000-$2,000; $100. Correct answer: $1,000-$2,000. Why: 100,000 × 0.01 to 0.02 = $1,000-$2,000. The percentages are illustrative assumptions, not a universal standard.
Why can an expiration payoff diagram understate account exposure? Options: It guarantees a profit; It includes all commissions; Assignment of one leg can leave a stock position; Spreads cannot lose. Correct answer: Assignment of one leg can leave a stock position. Why: The intact-spread payoff assumes both legs are resolved together. Assignment can create separate stock exposure and costs.

Answer notes
What does a journal prove on its own? Options: A profitable edge; Why the market moved; What observations and assumptions were recorded; A future win rate. Correct answer: What observations and assumptions were recorded. Why: The journal documents information; it does not prove causation or future returns.
In a hypothetical 2-unit order at $100 with a 0.1% buy fee, what cash is spent? Options: $200; $200.20; $210; $0.20. Correct answer: $200.20. Why: The $200 notional plus 0.1%, or $0.20, is $200.20.
Which sample should a review include? Options: Only gains; Only days with stable prices; Only large positions; Favorable and unfavorable cases under recorded rules. Correct answer: Favorable and unfavorable cases under recorded rules. Why: Selecting only attractive cases makes the summary misleading.
Does 30 recorded trades establish a reliable strategy? Options: No universal sample count can do that; Yes, always; Only with a journal; Only if there were no losing trades. Correct answer: No universal sample count can do that. Why: Sample design, costs, dependence and uncertainty matter.
